examples.en: If you add chili oil, the broth gets spicier and sharper.

examples.ko: 고추기름이 있으면 볶음 요리가 훨씬 맛있어요.
examples.en: With chili oil, stir-fried dishes taste much better.

examples.ko: 이 짬뽕은 고추기름 때문에 색이 빨개요.
examples.en: This jjamppong is red because of the chili oil.
If you fry garlic in chili oil, it smells great.
Does the mart near your home sell chili oil?

examples.ko: 너무 맵지 않게 고추기름은 조금만 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please add just a little chili oil so it's not too spicy.

explain: 짬뽕, 마파두부 같은 중국식 요리에 자주 나와요. 고춧가루와 달리 기름에 매운맛과 붉은 색이 우러난 것이라서 국물 위에 빨갛게 떠 있어요.
explain_en: It often appears in Chinese-style dishes such as jjamppong and mapo tofu. Unlike chili powder, the heat and red color are infused into the oil, so it floats red on top of the broth.

examples.ko: 이 생선은 뼈가 연해서 발라내지 않고 먹어도 돼요.
examples.en: This fish has soft bones, so you can eat it without removing them.

examples.ko: 아이를 위해 생선 가시를 꼼꼼히 발라냈어요.
examples.en: I carefully picked the bones out of the fish for the child.
I take the bones out of the chicken and stir-fry only the meat.
Peeling off the shrimp shells is a hassle.

examples.ko: 가시를 발라내 주시면 더 잘 먹을 것 같아요.
examples.en: If you pick out the bones for me, I think I'll eat better.
I bought only meat with the rib bones taken out.

explain: 뼈, 가시, 껍데기를 떼어 내고 먹을 살만 남길 때 써요. 생선, 고기, 새우나 게에 어울리고, '생선 살을 발라 먹다'처럼 '발라'만 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Used when you remove bones, fish bones or shells and keep only the edible meat. It suits fish, meat, shrimp and crab, and people often use just '발라', as in '생선 살을 발라 먹다'.

examples.ko: 돈가스를 만들 때 고기에 빵가루를 묻혀요.
examples.en: When making pork cutlets, you coat the meat with bread crumbs.

examples.ko: 빵가루가 없으면 식빵을 갈아서 써도 돼요.
examples.en: If you don't have bread crumbs, you can grind sandwich bread and use that.

examples.ko: 생선에 밀가루, 달걀, 빵가루 순서로 입혀 주세요.
examples.en: Please coat the fish with flour, egg, then bread crumbs in that order.

examples.ko: 빵가루는 기름에 튀기면 금방 갈색이 돼요.
examples.en: Bread crumbs turn brown quickly when fried in oil.

examples.ko: 장 보러 가서 달걀하고 빵가루도 샀어요.
examples.en: I went grocery shopping and bought eggs and bread crumbs too.

examples.ko: 빵가루 옷이 두꺼워서 안에 고기가 별로 없어요.
examples.en: The breading is so thick that there's hardly any meat inside.

explain: 돈가스나 튀김의 겉에 입히는 가루예요. '튀김옷'과 같이 알아 두면 좋고, '빵가루를 묻히다, 빵가루를 입히다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is the crumb coating put on pork cutlets and fried foods. It is good to learn it with '튀김옷' (batter coating), and you say '빵가루를 묻히다' or '빵가루를 입히다'.

examples.en: Lemon tea has a fresh, zesty taste.
The morning air is fresh, so I feel good.
I bought soap that has a fresh scent.
The outfit you're wearing today looks so fresh.

examples.ko: 느끼한 음식 뒤에는 상큼한 과일을 먹어요.
examples.en: After greasy food, I eat fresh, zesty fruit.
That child's smile is bright and cute.

explain: 신맛이 살짝 나는 과일, 향, 공기, 옷차림처럼 기분 좋게 산뜻한 것에 써요. '신선하다'는 오래되지 않았다는 뜻이고, '상큼하다'는 맛이나 느낌이 가볍고 깨끗하다는 뜻이에요. 특히 귤, 레몬, 딸기 같은 맛에 잘 써요.
explain_en: It fits pleasantly light things such as slightly tart fruit, scents, air, and outfits. 신선하다 says something is not stale, whereas 상큼하다 describes a light, clean taste or feeling. It is especially common for citrus and strawberries.

en: taste a sample; try a free sample

examples.en: A customer tried a sample of the new bread.
I tried a sample of the beef at the mart and bought it.

examples.ko: 먼저 시식하신 분이 맛을 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Whoever tasted it first, please tell us how it is.
I chose by sampling several kinds of kimchi.
The staff member gave me a small cup to sample.

examples.ko: 아이들은 시식할 수 있는 코너를 제일 좋아해요.
examples.en: Kids like the corner where they can sample food best.

explain: 마트나 가게에서 사기 전에 조금 먹어 보는 상황에 어울려요. 집에서 요리 맛을 보는 건 '맛보다'나 '간을 보다'라고 해요. 그냥 먹는 것은 '먹다'예요.
explain_en: It fits the situation of eating a little before buying at a mart or shop. Checking the taste of your own cooking at home is '맛보다' or '간을 보다'. Just eating is '먹다'.

examples.en: If you put crown daisy in the stew, it smells nice.
Crown daisy has a strong scent, so people either love or hate it.
I bought a bunch of crown daisy at the market.
I blanched the crown daisy lightly and seasoned it.
Fish cake soup feels lacking without crown daisy.
I eat crown daisy and lettuce together as a wrap.

explain: 이름에 '쑥'이 들어가지만 쑥과는 다른 채소예요. 탕, 찌개, 쌈에 향을 더하려고 넣는 경우가 많아요. 받침 ㅅ이 [ㄷ]으로 소리 나서 발음은 [쑥깓]이에요.
explain_en: Although it has '쑥' in its name, it is a different vegetable from mugwort. It is often added to soups, stews and wraps for aroma. The final ㅅ sounds like ㄷ, so it is pronounced [쑥깓].

examples.en: This summer the cherries in the yard ripened to a bright red.
I bought a bag of cherries at the market.
The baby's lips are small and red like cherries.

examples.ko: 앵두 철에는 할머니 댁 마당이 붉게 물들어요.
examples.en: In cherry season, my grandmother's yard turns red.
I tried making jam with cherries and it's tangy.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 마당에서 앵두를 따 먹곤 했어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I used to pick and eat cherries in the yard.

explain: 앵두는 작고 새콤한 빨간 열매예요. 마트에서 파는 크고 달콤한 열매는 보통 '체리'라고 불러서 서로 다르게 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 앵두 같은 입술로 유명해요.
phrases.en: That actress is famous for her cherry-red lips.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 붉고 예쁜 입술을 칭찬하는 비유예요. 조금 옛날 느낌이 나는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech praising small, red, pretty lips. It sounds a bit old-fashioned.

explain_en: 앵두 is a small, tart red fruit. The larger, sweeter fruit sold in supermarkets is usually called '체리', so the two names are used for different fruits.

examples.en: On a cold day I think of mushroom hot pot.
I ate beef hot pot with my family.
When the hot pot boils, add more vegetables.
This restaurant's tripe hot pot is delicious.

examples.ko: 전골 국물에 라면 사리를 넣어 먹었어요.
examples.en: I added instant noodles to the hot pot broth and ate it.

examples.ko: 손님이 오면 전골을 테이블 위에서 끓여요.
examples.en: When guests come, we boil the hot pot on the table.

explain: '전골'은 재료를 담은 냄비를 상 위에서 직접 끓이면서 먹는 요리예요. '찌개'는 주방에서 끓여 내오는 경우가 많은 것과 달라요. 재료가 풍성해서 같이 먹는 사람이 많을 때 시켜요.
explain_en: '전골' is a dish boiled right at the table as you eat, in a pot already filled with ingredients. '찌개' is often brought out already cooked from the kitchen, which is different. It is full of ingredients, so people order it when eating with a group.

examples.en: Milk has a lot of calcium.
Calcium is very good for your bones and teeth.
Anchovies also contain calcium.
If you lack calcium, your bones get weak.
The doctor told me to take calcium pills.
My grandmother gets her calcium from tofu.

explain: '칼슘이 풍부하다', '칼슘이 부족하다'처럼 '풍부하다·부족하다'와 자주 써요. 한국에서는 멸치, 우유, 두부가 칼슘이 많은 음식으로 유명해요. 약국에서 파는 영양제는 '칼슘제'라고 해요.
explain_en: It often pairs with '풍부하다' (abundant) and '부족하다' (lacking), as in '칼슘이 풍부하다'. In Korea anchovies, milk and tofu are famous calcium foods. A supplement from a pharmacy is called '칼슘제'.

examples.en: I like drinks with carbonation.
The fizz is gone, so it tastes flat.
Fizzy drinks are bad for your teeth.
I drank sparkling water with lemon.
The carbonation is strong, so my throat stings.

examples.ko: 저는 탄산을 못 마셔서 물을 시켜요.
examples.en: I can't drink fizzy drinks, so I order water.

explain: 원래는 화학 용어지만 일상에서는 콜라나 사이다 속 '톡 쏘는 거품'을 '탄산'이라고 불러요. '탄산음료', '탄산수'처럼 붙여 쓰고, '탄산이 세다/약하다/빠지다'로 정도를 말해요.
explain_en: Originally a chemistry term, in daily life it means the fizz in cola or soda. It joins into words like 탄산음료 and 탄산수, and you describe strength with 탄산이 세다, 약하다, or 빠지다.

en: relieving a hangover; eating a soup or having a drink for a hangover

examples.en: Hot soup is the best way to settle your stomach the next day.
People often eat bean sprout soup to settle the stomach.
The hangover soup restaurant had many customers from the morning.

examples.ko: 속이 안 좋을 때는 해장에 좋은 국물이 생각나요.
examples.en: When my stomach feels bad, I think of soup that's good for settling it.

examples.ko: 해장이 필요할 때는 따뜻한 국을 먹어요.
examples.en: When I need to settle my stomach, I eat a warm soup.

examples.ko: 한국 사람들은 해장을 위해 라면도 먹어요.
examples.en: Koreans also eat ramyeon to settle their stomachs.

explain: '해장국', '해장 라면'처럼 뒤에 음식 이름을 붙이는 경우가 많아요. 과음한 다음 날 속을 풀려고 먹는 따뜻한 국물 음식 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 식당 간판에서도 '해장국'이라는 말을 쉽게 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is often followed by a food name, as in '해장국' or '해장 라면'. It comes up in talk about warm, soupy food eaten the day after drinking too much to settle the stomach. You can easily see the word '해장국' on restaurant signs.
